ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, within the Cartesian coordinate system, the line AB passing through point A (4, 0) intersects with the y-axis at point B (0, 4). The parabola $y=-x^2+bx+c$ that passes through the origin O intersects the line AB at points A and C. The vertex of the parabola is D. What is the expression of the parabola $y=-x^2+bx+c$?
ready1_open_rewrite.title: MM-Math open-ended problem
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the diagram, within the Cartesian coordinate system, the line AB passing through point A (4, 0) intersects the y-axis at point B (0, 4). The parabola $y=-x^2+bx+c$ passes through the origin O and intersects line AB at points A and C. The vertex of the parabola is D. What is the expression of the parabola $y=-x^2+bx+c$?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: Solution: From the problem statement, we have \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} c=0\\ -16+4b+c=0 \end{array} \right. \] Solving this, we get \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} b=4\\ c=0 \end{array} \right. \] $\therefore$ The quadratic function is: \boxed{y=-x^{2}+4x}

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the diagram, within the Cartesian coordinate system, the line AB passing through point A (4, 0) intersects the y-axis at point B (0, 4). The parabola $y=-x^2+bx+c$ passes through the origin O and intersects line AB at points A and C. The vertex of the parabola is D. What is the expression of the parabola $y=-x^2+bx+c$?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Solution: From the problem statement, we have \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} c=0\\ -16+4b+c=0 \end{array} \right. \] Solving this, we get \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} b=4\\ c=0 \end{array} \right. \] $\therefore$ The quadratic function is: \boxed{y=-x^{2}+4x}
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows a Cartesian coordinate system with a downward-opening parabola passing through the origin O and the x-axis point A. A slanted line passes through A, crosses the y-axis at B, and intersects the parabola again at C. The vertex of the parabola is labeled D, with a dashed vertical line through it. Reasoning: The parabola has form y = -x^2 + bx + c. Since the parabola passes through O = (0,0), substituting gives 0 = 0 + 0 + c, so c = 0. Since the parabola also passes through A = (4,0), substituting gives 0 = -4^2 + 4b + c = -16 + 4b + c. With c = 0, this becomes 4b = 16, so b = 4. Therefore the parabola is y = -x^2 + 4x.
